sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Package overview and imports
sections.what: Describes the agent layer as specialists that each do one job and return checked data rather than prose. It then imports each specialist and the shared helpers from their files so they can be used from this one place.
sections.why: Stated in the docstring: shared machinery lives in one base file so the roster cannot drift agent by agent.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new agent here without updating the boundary notes in the authoring guide lets its must-not rules drift.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Public name list
sections.what: Lists the names this package promises to other code, covering the agents, the shared errors and base classes, the helpers and the model tier type.
sections.why: Likely reason: it makes the supported entry points explicit. The code does not say more.
sections.watch_out: A name missing from this list can still be imported from its own file, but it is not promised as public, so keep the list in step when adding agents.

summary: The package entry point for the agent layer. It imports each specialist agent and shared helper, and lists the names other code may use.
purpose: Give the rest of the system one place to import agents and their shared machinery from.
why: The docstring says the shared retry, budget, citation and boundary logic lives in one base file so the agents cannot drift apart. This file only gathers them.
how: 1) The module docstring describes the agent layer and points to the authoring guide. 2) Imports pull in the shared base classes and errors, the routing helpers, the prompt helpers and each specialist. 3) A list of names declares what is public.
inputs: None at runtime. It is read when the package is imported.
outputs: Names for other modules to import, such as the specialist agents and the shared base classes.
risks: Importing this package loads every agent, so a broken import in one agent file breaks all of them. A new agent that is not listed here is still importable from its own file but is not part of the public list.
debug: If importing an agent fails with a missing name, check that the name is spelled the same here and in its file. If an import loop appears, check which module imports which.
